title: VP of Product Development

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: As a Fortune 500 materials manufacturer producing their own protective films with 5-12 year outdoor durability claims, the VP of Product Development owns product portfolio strategy and competitive differentiation in a crowded market against 3M, HP, and other major players. Tedlar's 12-20+ year proven lifespan and superior UV/graffiti resistance represents a potential technology licensing opportunity or co-development partnership that would extend Avery Dennison's premium product line and deliver measurably better warranty performance. This role cares about: (1) extending product lifespan beyond current 12-year max to capture ultra-premium architectural and transit segments, (2) reducing warranty claims from UV degradation and cracking that impact brand reputation, (3) differentiating from 3M's Scotchcal and other competitive wrapping films through provable 20+ year performance data. Given Avery Dennison's massive fleet projects (30,000 DPD vehicles) and architectural applications, a protective overlaminate with Tedlar's graffiti-cleaning properties could become a value-added upsell layer for their Supreme Wrapping Film line, addressing customer pain points around vandalism on high-visibility transit and building wraps.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: This VP owns the entire product portfolio strategy for Avery Dennison's Graphics Solutions division, making critical decisions on materials technology, product line architecture, and competitive positioning. They likely report to the President of Graphics Solutions and oversee R&D, product management, and technical engineering teams. Their authority extends to technology partnerships, licensing agreements, and strategic decisions about which performance tiers to offer in vehicle wrapping films, architectural films, and protective solutions. With Avery Dennison's current maximum outdoor lifespan at 12 years, this role has the mandate and budget to explore technologies that extend performance into the 15-20+ year range to capture ultra-premium segments.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: The most relevant Tedlar application for this role is as a protective overlaminate layer that sits atop Avery Dennison's existing Supreme Wrapping Film and architectural graphic products. Specifically: (1) Fleet Graphics Enhancement - For massive projects like the 30,000-vehicle DPD fleet wrap, a Tedlar overlaminate would extend the current 5-10 year lifespan and add graffiti resistance, reducing maintenance costs for fleet customers and creating a premium upsell opportunity. (2) Architectural Facade Systems - In building wraps and architectural panels where Avery Dennison competes for municipal and commercial contracts, Tedlar's proven exterior performance and mold/mildew resistance would enable 20-year warranties that currently aren't achievable with cast vinyl alone. (3) Transit Interior Applications - Tedlar's -70°F to 230°F operating range and graffiti-cleaning properties make it ideal for bus/rail interiors where Avery Dennison's current products face vandalism and extreme temperature challenges. The value proposition isn't replacing their existing films but augmenting them to create a new performance tier.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: This VP's success metrics center on: (1) Product line profitability and margin expansion through premium tier offerings, (2) Market share gains in high-value segments (architectural, transit, premium fleet) where 3M and specialty competitors currently win on durability specifications, (3) Warranty claim reduction and customer satisfaction scores, particularly around UV degradation and premature fading complaints that damage brand reputation. They personally face pressure to differentiate Avery Dennison's 90-year vinyl heritage in a commoditizing market where Chinese manufacturers compete on price. Tedlar's documented 60+ year track record and graffiti resistance solve a critical pain point: enabling this VP to offer provable 20-year outdoor warranties that open doors to municipal transit contracts, Fortune 500 corporate fleet accounts, and architectural specification documents that currently require performance beyond what cast vinyl can deliver. The graffiti-cleaning capability specifically addresses complaints from the DPD fleet project and similar high-visibility installations where vandalism drives costly premature replacements.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: Avery Dennison just exhibited at ISA International Sign Expo 2025 in April, celebrating 90 years in vinyl graphic films—a milestone that creates internal momentum for innovation investments that honor their heritage while pushing performance boundaries. The company is also fresh off completing the massive 30,000-vehicle DPD fleet wrap project, which likely generated real-world performance data and customer feedback about durability needs in extreme-use fleet applications. With ISA Sign Expo 2026 planning already underway and FESPA events on the horizon, there's strategic timing to explore a technology partnership that could be showcased as next-generation innovation at these industry events. Additionally, the competitive pressure from 3M, HP, and emerging manufacturers exhibiting alongside Avery Dennison at FESPA Middle East 2024 creates urgency to differentiate with breakthrough performance claims.

personalization_hooks.hook: Avery Dennison's Supreme Wrapping Film currently maxes out at 12-year outdoor performance for black/white applications, creating a ceiling for ultra-premium architectural and transit segments that demand 15-20+ year warranties
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Open by acknowledging their industry-leading 12-year performance, then position Tedlar as the technology layer that breaks through that ceiling—enabling a new 'Platinum Series' with documented 20+ year warranties for municipal transit contracts and architectural facade projects where they're currently losing specification battles to specialty PVF solutions

personalization_hooks.hook: The 30,000-vehicle DPD fleet project represents massive scale but also exposes vulnerability to graffiti vandalism and premature replacement costs that impact customer retention and total cost of ownership positioning
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Reference their DPD fleet success as proof of installation scale capability, then introduce Tedlar's graffiti-cleaning properties (spray paint and permanent marker removal) as a value-added overlaminate that transforms fleet graphics from consumable to capital investment—reducing replacement frequency and creating premium upsell opportunity for transit and municipal fleet customers

personalization_hooks.hook: With 90 years in vinyl films and active competition against 3M's Scotchcal at ISA and FESPA events, product differentiation requires provable performance data that withstands competitive scrutiny from technical buyers and architects
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Lead with respect for their 90-year heritage in vinyl technology, then position Tedlar's 60+ year proven track record as complementary legacy that validates a strategic partnership—offering third-party tested performance data and case studies that support premium positioning against 3M while opening architectural and transit segments where current cast vinyl chemistry reaches performance limits

recommended_approach: Lead with product portfolio strategy and premium tier expansion opportunity. Frame Tedlar not as a replacement for their existing technology but as a strategic overlaminate layer that extends Avery Dennison's product line into ultra-premium segments (architectural facades, municipal transit, high-visibility fleet graphics) where their current 12-year maximum creates a competitive ceiling. Position the conversation as a technology partnership exploration rather than a vendor pitch—emphasizing how Tedlar's graffiti resistance and 20+ year performance data solve specific pain points from real-world projects like the DPD fleet installation. Reference their ISA presence and 90-year milestone to create peer-level positioning between two materials science companies with proven track records.
